reasons: The rule is correctly triggered: Section 7 has only a heading referencing indemnification (and in Contractor's favour at that) with no operative indemnity language, and the cited limitation-of-liability/attorneys'-fee provisions confirm no Vendor defence obligation exists — this is the walk-away scenario for a critical rule.

The inserted Section 7(d) tracks the playbook preferred position closely: IP infringement, breach of law, Contractor-caused unauthorised access/disclosure of Company data, and gross negligence/wilful misconduct, plus standard notice, control-of-defence (with consent for adverse settlements) and cooperation procedure.

Placement is consistent with the redline guidance (appended after the limitation-of-liability subsections as a new 7(d)) and is additive only — no existing language is deleted or distorted, so the edit is the smallest one that reaches the position.

No Customer/Company indemnity exists in the cited text, so the rationale's statement that nothing needs narrowing is accurate; the carve-out from the Section 7(a) cap and 7(c) fee waiver is necessary for the indemnity to have practical effect and is a coherent ask given 7(a) already excepts Paragraph 9.

Comment is accurate, in the required voice with the [Playbook] prefix, states what changed and why, and offers the documented fallback (usual IP exclusions, procure/modify/replace/refund, 3x annual fees super-cap).

Minor, non-blocking drafting points to confirm on cleanup: the clause uses the capitalised term "Works" (verify it is defined in the agreement, otherwise use "deliverables" as used in Section 1(a)), and the Section 7 heading "INDEMNIFICATION OF CONTRACTOR" should be conformed to reflect the new Contractor-side obligation.
